$comment: The sections of the libraries rule. The setup skill asks one question per section; apply.mjs writes the rule from the answers. platform: what to use without a library, always in the rule. use: follows the library's name on its line. notes: rules that hold while a library is chosen. An option's packages find it in package.json (a name ending in / matches a whole scope); when says when to pick it. The answer is an option id, none, or any other name the user gave.

sections.title: Components
sections.platform: a plain `<button>` for toggles, a native `<select>` for a short list of options.
sections.use: for menus, popovers, windows, confirmations, radio groups, bottom panels and search suggestions. The platform covers only part of these: focus, keyboard navigation and positioning stay on you.

options.name: Base UI
options.when: New projects: one library with every component, unstyled, including search suggestions.

options.name: Radix
options.when: Longest record and widest use, but no ready suggestions field.

options.name: React Aria
options.when: Accessibility and many languages come first; a larger download.

sections.title: Forms
sections.platform: a native `<form>`, enough for a few independent fields.
sections.use: , when a form has many fields, fields that depend on each other, fields added at runtime, or errors per field as the user types. It uses the same schema as the server.

options.name: React Hook Form
options.when: The common default, with the widest use.

options.name: TanStack Form
options.when: Strict types and async validation out of the box.

options.name: Conform
options.when: Forms on server actions that also work without JavaScript.

sections.title: Validation
sections.platform: field attributes help the user; they protect nothing, as the server can get any request.
sections.use: for data from outside the code: request bodies, server action arguments, query values. Do not check these by hand or cast them.
notes: Validate at the edge of a route or action; code behind it gets typed data and does not check again.
Keep the library out of client code unless a form needs it, so the browser does not download it.
Validate a third-party API's response only where a wrong answer would do real harm.

options.name: Zod
options.when: The common default, and most libraries connect to it.

options.name: Valibot
options.when: Validation runs in the browser and its download matters.

sections.title: URL state
sections.platform: `URLSearchParams` for building a one-off link or an address for a request.
sections.use: for filters and anything else that reads and changes the page's query parameters. Check that it works with the framework's caching before relying on it.
notes: Changes that wait for a button, such as Apply in a panel, stay in local state until it is pressed.

options.name: nuqs
options.when: Pages with filters: typed parameters on client and server.

sections.title: Data
sections.platform: a single request from the browser with nothing shared or saved around it is a plain `fetch`.
sections.use: for data in the browser: next pages of a list, search suggestions, data shared by many components, and every write that shows at once. In an app without server rendering, for all server data.
notes: Do not write rollback by hand; a failed write puts the old data back through the library.
Writes to one item run in order, so quick clicks cannot race.
Do not fetch in `useEffect` when a query fits.

options.name: TanStack Query
options.when: The common default: paging, writes with rollback and shared cache.

options.name: SWR
options.when: Mostly reading data; a smaller download and fewer features.

options.name: RTK Query
options.when: The project is built on Redux.

sections.title: Client state
sections.platform: the URL for what a link should keep, `useState` for one component, Context for a few components under one provider. Data from the server does not go in a hand-written store.
sections.use: , when state is shared by distant components and Context re-renders are measured as a real slowdown.

options.name: Zustand
options.when: One small store, the simplest choice.

options.name: Jotai
options.when: Many small independent pieces of state.

options.name: Redux Toolkit
options.when: Large apps with strict patterns, or Redux is already there.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.platform: an error shows in place as `role="alert"`, through one shared component.
sections.use: , when a message must outlive the place it came from. Do not add a second toast library.

options.name: Base UI
options.when: Components come from Base UI, so nothing new to add.

options.name: Sonner
options.when: Components come from elsewhere; ready-made look.

sections.title: Dates and numbers
sections.use: , only for calculations these cannot do, such as time zone arithmetic.

options.name: date-fns
options.when: Plain functions over `Date`; only what is imported is downloaded.

options.name: Day.js
options.when: Moving from Moment: nearly the same API.
